items.followUp: Explain the population level and ecosystem level of biological organization.

rubric.why: The organism level refers to one individual living thing.
rubric.description: Defines the organism level as an individual living thing.
rubric.how: Award both marks for clearly identifying it as one individual organism.

rubric.why: A community consists of populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.
rubric.description: Defines a community and explains its essential features.
rubric.how: Award one mark for populations of different species, one for the same area or habitat, and one for interaction.

modelAnswer: Organism level: An organism is an individual living thing, such as a plant or an animal.
Community level: A community consists of populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.

rubric.why: A prokaryotic cell lacks a membrane-bound nucleus, whereas a eukaryotic cell has one.
rubric.description: Compares the presence of a nucleus.
rubric.how: Award the mark for the correct contrast.

rubric.why: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles, while eukaryotes contain them.
rubric.description: Compares membrane-bound organelles.
rubric.how: Award the mark for the correct contrast.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic DNA is generally circular and not enclosed in a nucleus; eukaryotic DNA is arranged in linear chromosomes associated with proteins.
rubric.description: Compares the genetic material.
rubric.how: Award the mark for a correct contrast in DNA or chromosome organization.

rubric.why: Bacteria are prokaryotes; plants, animals, and fungi are eukaryotes.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of each cell type.
rubric.how: Award the mark when examples of both types are correctly identified.

modelAnswer: Prokaryotic cells have no membrane-bound nucleus; eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells contain them.
Prokaryotic DNA is generally circular and not enclosed in a nucleus; eukaryotic DNA forms linear chromosomes associated with proteins.
Bacteria are prokaryotes, whereas plant, animal, and fungal cells are eukaryotic.

items.followUp: Describe how temperature and substrate concentration affect enzyme action.

rubric.why: Enzyme activity rises with temperature up to an optimum, then falls as the enzyme's structure is disrupted at higher temperatures.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of temperature on enzyme action.
rubric.how: Award one mark for the increase to an optimum and one for the decrease/denaturation above it.

rubric.why: Each enzyme works best at an optimum pH; a pH change alters the active site or enzyme structure and reduces its activity.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of pH on enzyme action.
rubric.how: Award one mark for an optimum pH, one for the effect of a pH change on the enzyme/active site, and one for reduced activity or denaturation.

modelAnswer: Temperature: As temperature rises, enzyme activity increases up to an optimum temperature.
Above the optimum temperature, the enzyme's structure is disrupted (denatured), so its activity decreases.
pH: Each enzyme has an optimum pH at which it works fastest.
A pH above or below the optimum alters the enzyme's active site or structure, reducing its activity and possibly denaturing it.

items.followUp: Describe how fermentation is used in bread-making and in the production of yoghurt.

rubric.why: Fermentation is an anaerobic process; yeast breaks down glucose to form ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.description: States the process and a fermentation product.
rubric.how: Award the mark for identifying anaerobic breakdown by yeast and its products.

rubric.why: Carbon dioxide produced by yeast makes bread dough rise.
rubric.description: Explains fermentation in bread-making.
rubric.how: Award the mark for linking carbon dioxide to rising dough.

rubric.why: Yeast fermentation is used to produce alcoholic beverages.
rubric.description: Identifies fermentation's role in producing alcoholic drinks.
rubric.how: Award the mark for naming alcoholic drink or ethanol production.

rubric.why: Bacteria ferment sugars to lactic acid in the production of yoghurt and some cheeses.
rubric.description: Identifies fermentation in dairy-food production.
rubric.how: Award the mark for linking bacteria/lactic acid fermentation with yoghurt or cheese.

modelAnswer: Fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose; yeast produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
In bread-making, carbon dioxide produced by yeast makes the dough rise.
Yeast fermentation is also used to produce alcoholic drinks such as beer and wine.
Lactic acid bacteria ferment sugars to make yoghurt and some cheeses.

items.followUp: Explain how guard cells cause stomata to open and close.

rubric.why: In light, photosynthesis in guard cells increases the concentration of their cell sap.
rubric.description: Explains the change in guard cells in light.
rubric.how: Award the mark for linking light/photosynthesis to increased cell-sap concentration.

rubric.why: Water enters the guard cells by osmosis, making them turgid and opening the stomatal pore.
rubric.description: Explains stomatal opening.
rubric.how: Award the mark for the water-entry/turgidity mechanism and opening.

rubric.why: In darkness, sugar in guard cells is converted to starch and the cell-sap concentration decreases.
rubric.description: Explains the change in guard cells in darkness.
rubric.how: Award the mark for linking darkness to reduced cell-sap concentration.

rubric.why: Water leaves the guard cells, making them flaccid and closing the stomatal pore.
rubric.description: Explains stomatal closing.
rubric.how: Award the mark for the water-loss/flaccidity mechanism and closing.

modelAnswer: In light, photosynthesis in guard cells increases the concentration of their cell sap.
Water enters the guard cells by osmosis; they become turgid and the stomata open.
In darkness, sugar in guard cells is converted to starch, lowering the concentration of their cell sap.
Water leaves the guard cells by osmosis; they become flaccid and the stomata close.

items.followUp: Name one contribution made by Jabir bin Hayan to science.

rubric.why: Jabir bin Hayan is known as the father of chemistry.
rubric.description: Identifies his association with chemistry.
rubric.how: Award the mark for naming him as the father of chemistry or identifying chemistry as his field.

rubric.why: He is associated with the development of experimental methods in chemistry.
rubric.description: States his contribution to experimental science.
rubric.how: Award the mark for mentioning the experimental method or chemical experimentation.

modelAnswer: Jabir bin Hayan was a famous Muslim scientist known as the father of chemistry.
He contributed to the development of experimental methods in chemistry.

items.followUp: Give one reason why measurements made with instruments are useful in biology.

rubric.why: Quantitative observations express results as numerical measurements.
rubric.description: States that quantitative observations provide numerical measurements.
rubric.how: Award the mark for identifying the use of numbers or measurements.

rubric.why: Numerical measurements are more precise and objective, so they can be compared more reliably than descriptive observations.
rubric.description: Explains why quantitative observations are more accurate or useful.
rubric.how: Award the mark for a valid explanation such as greater precision, objectivity, or reliable comparison.

modelAnswer: Quantitative observations give results as numerical measurements.
These measurements are more precise and objective than descriptions, so they can be compared more reliably.

items.followUp: What is a variable in an experiment, and why should only one variable be changed at a time?

rubric.why: A control provides a standard for comparison with the experimental results.
rubric.description: Defines the control in an experiment.
rubric.how: Award the mark for identifying it as a comparison or standard.

rubric.why: In a controlled experiment, other conditions are kept constant while the tested variable is changed.
rubric.description: Explains the purpose or arrangement of a control.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that conditions are kept the same except for the variable being tested.

modelAnswer: A control is the standard or comparison used to judge the results of an experiment.
All conditions are kept the same except for the one variable being tested.
